title: POC Weekly Sync - Benchmark Results Review vs Baseline
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark latency and throughput vs customer baseline (OpenAI). Redwood showed lower median latency and higher throughput in tuned Dedicated configs; KV caching and batching materially reduced p95. Agreed next steps: customer to share representative prompts, Redwood to run production-like pass and enable dedicated pool trial.
topics: Impact of batching and KV caching
Cost estimates and pricing for Dedicated
Next steps for canary and production run

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-02-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (NovaRetail - Head of ML), Aisha Khan (NovaRetail - Infra), Dmitri Petrov (NovaRetail - Product)
Links shared: benchmark spreadsheet (drive.redwood/novaretail-bench-2025-02-10), perf dashboard (console.redwood/reports/74219), security packet (docs.redwood/security.pdf)

[00:00] Jordan: Okay hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick check — can you all see my screen? I'm pulling up the benchmark summary.
[00:22] Carlos: Yep we can see it, looks good. Thanks.
[00:30] Jordan: Great. Quick agenda: review the numbers we ran last week vs your baseline on OpenAI, talk through tuning we did (batching, KV cache, quantization), call out regressions, and agree next steps for a dedicated trial. Sound good?
[00:45] Aisha: Sounds good. We especially care about p95 — production SLO is 500ms for our 256-token prompts.
[00:52] Priya: Noted. We'll highlight p50 and p95 and also the throughput under sustained load.
[01:05] Jordan: Alright first slide — baseline: NovaRetail ran their workload against OpenAI hosted API with a 256 token prompt average. Their reported numbers were p50 420ms, p95 760ms, throughput ~12 requests/sec under the 16-concurrent-worker test. Cost estimate they gave was around $0.60 per 1k tokens for their call pattern.
[01:40] Carlos: That's correct, those were our numbers from last week's run.
[01:44] Jordan: Redwood hosted (default config) we measured p50 270ms, p95 460ms, throughput ~18 req/sec under the same harness. So about 35% lower median latency and ~1.5x throughput.
[02:10] Dmitri: That's a nice delta. Where's that coming from? Different model or inference runtime?
[02:18] Priya: Mainly runtime and batching—our serving runtime does continuous batching and optimized kernels for attention patterns. We also used a 16-bit quantized variant for that run which reduces compute. There is a quality tradeoff we validated — no obvious regressions on your eval set but we'll continue to check.
[02:38] Jordan: Next, we ran a dedicated pool config with KV cache enabled and larger batching; results were p50 160ms, p95 310ms, throughput ~28 req/sec. This is the config we'd suggest for a production canary.
[02:58] Carlos: Wait so dedicated + KV cache drops p95 from 460 to 310? That's good. Any stability issues under longer runs?
[03:07] Priya: Under a sustained 30-minute test with 100 concurrent workers we saw stable latencies; memory growth was bounded thanks to eviction policies. There was one hiccup at 23 minutes correlated with a GC spike on the host image — we captured logs and it was transient.
[03:26] Aisha: Can you share those logs? We need to see host-level metrics for our infra team.
[03:31] Jordan: Yes — spreadsheet includes raw logs and we've put a link to the perf dashboard.
[03:36] Priya: On the KV cache: for chat-style workloads where prefixes repeat across requests, we get a large p95 improvement because we avoid recomputing early layers. For your workload about 42% of requests benefited from prefix cache in our sample traces.
[03:56] Carlos: Interesting. Our prompts have a fair bit of overlap — product description + user messages. That sounds promising.
[04:03] Dmitri: Any accuracy impact when using quantized models? We care about downstream NLU and classification thresholds.
[04:10] Priya: The 16-bit quantized variant had negligible diffs on our automated eval for your 2k test-set (f1 delta < 0.5%), but for edge-case hallucination checks some rare prompts show small changes. We recommended running the same eval on your full set.
[04:28] Jordan: Cost-wise: using Dedicated reduces per-token cost in our model — rough numbers from the run: Redwood dedicated config estimated $0.28 per 1k tokens equivalent in this test (including infra amortization in the POC), whereas your baseline with OpenAI came in at ~$0.60 per 1k tokens. These are estimates, we will provide detailed breakdown in the spreadsheet.
[04:56] Carlos: That's compelling. For procurement we still need compliance stuff — SOC2, audit logs, KMS integration.
[05:04] Jordan: Yep, we shared the security packet link earlier — it includes SOC 2 Type II, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integration notes. For the private/VPC trial we can run a short checklist and support engineer assist with whitelisting.
[05:23] Aisha: We'll need CIDR ranges for the trial and guidance on egress.
[05:29] Priya: We'll put together a minimal network plan; Jordan will follow up with a request for IPs.
[05:36] Carlos: Back to performance — what about long-context scenarios? We do some 4k+ prompts occasionally.
[05:43] Priya: Good question. Our initial runs were 256-token avg; we did a smaller experiment at 2048 tokens and saw p95 increase as expected: dedicated config p95 rose to ~680ms for 2k context vs baseline OpenAI at ~920ms in your tests. KV cache is less effective for unique long contexts. We recommended trying prefix chunking and partial cache eviction for those cases.
[06:10] Jordan: We also looked at batching knobs — increasing batch window from 8ms to 15ms improved throughput further (roughly +20%) but added ~20ms median latency; tradeoff depends on SLO tolerances.
[06:24] Dmitri: For our use case we can tolerate slightly higher median if p95 stays under 500ms.
[06:30] Jordan: Then the recommended config is: Dedicated pool, KV cache on, batching window 10ms, and the 16-bit quantized model. That hit p95 ~310ms in our run.
[06:44] Carlos: What about failsafe? If dedicated capacity is saturated can we fallback to hosted?
[06:50] Priya: Yes; smart routing can fall back to a compatible hosted variant — we can set an automatic fallback policy per route to preserve availability.
[06:59] Aisha: How do rollouts work - canary vs full? We want to test on 5% of traffic first.
[07:06] Jordan: Console supports canary/AB with automatic rollback rules based on latency and error thresholds. We'll help configure the first canary.
[07:14] Carlos: Any regressions you saw in the week-to-week runs?
[07:18] Priya: A couple of small things: one experiment used an aggressive quantization (8-bit) which dropped some classification metrics beyond our threshold; we reverted that and did 16-bit instead. There was also a misconfigured batch script that temporarily inflated concurrency during one run — logs flagged it.
[07:36] Jordan: All fixed — notes in the spreadsheet.
[07:40] Dmitri: For the dedicated trial, what's the minimum commit? We need to justify cost to finance.
[07:47] Jordan: For a short pilot we can do a time-limited reserved pool with no long-term commitment — it's available as a trial for a few weeks. Production reservations start at monthly commitments but we'll send a pricing note.
[07:59] Carlos: OK good. Next — can we run a production-like pass with our actual data?
[08:05] Priya: Yes, we recommend 2k representative prompts and run them at your typical concurrency for 4 hours to measure steady-state p95.
[08:14] Jordan: Action: Carlos to share testset + PII policy. Jordan will run a dedicated trial with KV cache and post raw logs + perf dashboard.
[08:24] Aisha: We'll also need a brief runbook on incident triage and support contacts.
[08:30] Jordan: We'll include that in the packet.
[08:33] Carlos: Great. Side question: we saw mention of Anthropic in your doc — how do those numbers compare?
[08:39] Priya: Anthropic numbers are similar to OpenAI in many emerging benchmarks but we didn't run Anthropic in this POC. If you want a 3-way comparison we can schedule that.
[08:50] Dmitri: Not necessary this week, maybe later.
[08:53] Jordan: Cool. Any other concerns?
[08:56] Carlos: Latency percentiles under tail spikes — can we get tracing for those spikes?
[09:02] Priya: Yes we have per-request traces and token-level timing; we'll share a sample trace that shows the GC spike and the token-level breakdown.
[09:11] Jordan: Quick recap of concrete numbers in the sheet: Baseline (OpenAI): p50 420ms / p95 760ms / throughput ~12 rps. Redwood hosted (default): p50 270ms / p95 460ms / throughput ~18 rps. Redwood Dedicated + KV+batching: p50 160ms / p95 310ms / throughput ~28 rps.
[09:36] Carlos: Thanks. That's clear.
[09:40] Aisha: One more infra ask — if we do private deployment (VPC) how long to stand up?
[09:45] Priya: For a customer trial we can do a VPC private deployment in about 2 weeks with cooperation on networking and KMS. On-prem air-gapped takes longer.
[09:54] Dmitri: Ok we can prioritize VPC then.
[09:57] Jordan: Great. Let's confirm owners and dates — Jordan will send the spreadsheet and logs by Friday (2025-02-14). Priya will run the 95th-percentile stress test and post updated numbers by 2025-02-19. Customer to provide prompt set and network constraints by the dates in the action items.
[10:19] Carlos: Sounds good.
[10:22] Jordan: Any final Qs?
[10:24] Dmitri: None here.
[10:25] Aisha: All good.
[10:27] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the dedicated trial and the shared docs.
[10:33] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words and speaker attribution approximated; see attachments for exact logs and perf traces.
